## Natural history notes

A small owlet moth characterized by brown to grayish-brown forewings with pale curved markings, including a whitish “U”-shaped mark that gives the species part of its scientific name. In Florida, it is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, and other areas with suitable host plants and resting cover. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars are plant borers or concealed feeders, developing within stems or related plant tissues and serving as part of the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
